messages:
jordan: Hey team — Enterprise customer (acct: acme-inc) reporting a persistent re-auth loop after MFA. They say users are prompted for MFA every ~10 minutes even when 'Remember this device' is checked. Happening across Chrome and Edge. Not seeing 5xx errors in app logs, auth failures look like missing session cookie. Filing here so we have a thread.

jordan: Customer provided one repro: user logs in via SSO -> completes MFA -> gets redirected back to app. After ~10 mins any navigation triggers redirect to SSO again. Cookie set on login looks normal per their screenshot.

maria_s: Thanks, @jordan — can you attach their Set-Cookie header and an example Redirect URL? Also which SSO provider (Okta/Azure/GitHub)?

jordan: Provider is Okta. They pasted the Set-Cookie from browser devtools: 

```
Set-Cookie: rw_session=eyJhbGciOi...; Path=/; Domain=acme.example.com; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=600
```

jordan: Note Max-Age is 600s (10m). Customer thinks setting "remember device" should extend this.

tyler_ops: Uh — Max-Age=600 explains the 10m. Where is Max-Age set? In session service or SSO callback?

emily_platform: App's session service sets short lifetime for default sessions (10m) and upgrades to 30d when we set device_trust=true and we set a separate persistent cookie `device_trust` with longer expiry. Sounds like the upgrade to persistent session didn't happen for these users.

maria_s: Do we have logs showing device_trust cookie being set? @sre_oncall can you check auth-proxy logs for `SET_COOKIE device_trust` events for acme-inc users around their login times?

sre_oncall: Pulling logs now. I grep'd for acme user ids mentioned in support ticket. I see successful `SET_COOKIE rw_session` entries but I don't see `SET_COOKIE device_trust` in the last 24h for their tenant. Sample log lines: 

```
2025-07-20T15:12:05Z auth-callback INFO user=acct-789 set rw_session; max_age=600
2025-07-20T15:12:05Z auth-callback INFO user=acct-789 redirect=/app/dashboard
```

sre_oncall: No device_trust creation step. Either the SSO assertion didn't include the flag or our device-trust flow failed.

maria_s: Do we enforce SameSite policies on `device_trust` cookie? Browser changes in late 2024 started treating third-party contexts differently. If the SSO redirect flows through a different host, SameSite=Lax could prevent the persistent cookie from being set.

jordan: Customer said they use a small iframe in their SSO callback for a post-login handshake to set the device cookie. That could be blocked by SameSite/Lax.

tyler_ops: That matches. If the iframe does POST or navigational cross-site, the cookie won't be set unless SameSite=None; Secure is required too.

emily_platform: Confirmed in our cookie code we default device_trust SameSite to Lax unless `cross_site_flow=true` feature flag is enabled for the tenant. acme-inc doesn't have the flag. Looks like our change to default Lax (safer) broke older SSO iframe setups.

maria_s: Repro steps for engineering (short):
1) Create test tenant with Okta SSO configured (use acme test creds)
2) Login -> finish MFA
3) In SSO callback flow, emulate iframe handshake that POSTs to /auth/device-trust with no top-level navigation
4) Observe cookie set attempt in response headers (curl -I or browser devtools)

```
# reproduce via curl (example):
curl -i -X POST 'https://acme.example.com/auth/device-trust' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"trust":true}' -b 'rw_session=eyJ...'
```

maria_s: If step 4 fails and response includes Set-Cookie but browser doesn't store it, that's SameSite/Lax blocking.

sre_oncall: Quick mitigation: enable the `cross_site_flow` feature flag for acme-inc which will set `SameSite=None; Secure` for device_trust. That should allow iframe-set cookies. Patch has been tested in staging.

jordan: Customer okayed enabling feature flag for a small pilot. Can we also increase default Max-Age for device_trust cookie to 30d when trust=true? They expect "Remember this device" to last weeks, not 10m.

emily_platform: Yes — device_trust cookie already uses 30d in codepath but the problem is it never got created. After flag flip we'll see the long-lived cookie created. We should also add telemetry event `device_trust.created` to measure rollouts.

tyler_ops: Two additional concerns: 1) Some browsers drop cookies if cookie header > 4096 bytes or if there are too many cookies for the domain. Customer has several legacy cookies on `acme.example.com` from older apps. If they hit the limit our device_trust might be silently dropped. 2) If the iframe is cross-site and blocked by browser ITP/privacy settings, SameSite=None alone may not be sufficient.

maria_s: Good catch. Let's include these in troubleshooting notes and ask customer to check devtools > Storage > Cookies to confirm device_trust exists after pilot. Also ask them to clear old cookies if they suspect size limit.

sre_oncall: Action plan: 
- [P0] Enable `cross_site_flow` flag for acme-inc tonight at 02:00 UTC (small pilot).
- [P1] Monitor auth-proxy logs for `SET_COOKIE device_trust` and new telemetry event.
- [P1] If successful, schedule tenant-wide change to default `SameSite=None` for device_trust and add server-side fallback to set a top-level redirect-based persistent cookie when iframe set fails.

jordan: I'll update the customer with the pilot time and ask them to verify. Also asked them to provide a HAR file from an affected user session and a screenshot of devtools Storage tab.

emily_platform: One more note for eng: when adding telemetry, include fields: tenant_id, user_id, method (iframe|top_redirect), result (success|blocked), user_agent. Will help triage browser-specific issues.

maria_s: If pilot fails or customer sees other symptoms (e.g., immediate 401s with `token_expired` vs reauth loop), escalate to SRE for token validation checks — but current evidence points to cookie never being set rather than session expiring early.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-3321 assigned to @sre_oncall; priority P1 for pilot monitoring.

jordan: Thanks everyone — I'll post updates after customer verifies post-flag. :thumbsup:
